49	//    at the call sites and run the §5.4 go/no-go gate.
50	//
51	//  WHY offset-based symmetric addressing (not raw pointers): NVSHMEM's
52	//  symmetric heap guarantees the SAME offset is valid on every PE
53	//  (nvshmem_malloc returns symmetric addresses; nvshmem_ptr(sym, pe) translates
54	//  for NVLink load/store). The loopback reproduces exactly that property with
55	//  base + pe*stride. One addressing model ⇒ one math code path.
56	//
57	//  DETERMINISM (design §5.2, non-negotiable): the fixed-order all-reduce below
58	//  reads every PE's partial in ASCENDING pe order and accumulates fp32. The
59	//  summation order is STRUCTURAL (never timing-dependent), so the result is
60	//  bit-identical on every PE and across reruns — the cross-rank analogue of the
61	//  in-kernel ascending-CTA reduce that made the single-GPU path A/A/A.
62	//  A `nvshmem_float_sum_reduce` collective is deliberately NOT used (its
63	//  reduction order is unspecified) — on NVSHMEM the same ascending-pe loop runs
64	//  over nvshmem_ptr-translated peer pointers (NVLink direct load/store).
65	// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
66	//
67	// HEADER-ONLY, self-contained: CUDA runtime + the GridBarrier substrate only.
68	// No torch, no NCCL. Compiles for sm_90a with plain nvcc.

85	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
86	//  LoopbackTransport — single-process symmetric-heap simulation (the 1-GPU
87	//  honest test transport). See the swap-point doc above.
88	//
89	//  Host side: allocate ONE device buffer of `n_pes * stride_floats` floats and
90	//  pass (base, stride_floats, n_pes). Device side: each CTA derives its virtual
91	//  pe from its blockIdx (contiguous CTA groups per PE — `pe_of_cta`).
92	//  The rendezvous is the caller's whole-grid GridBarrier (all virtual PEs share
93	//  the grid), so `rendezvous()` simply forwards to bar.sync().
94	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
95	struct LoopbackTransport {
96	    float*  heap_base;       // [n_pes * stride_floats] device alloc
97	    int64_t stride_floats;   // per-PE symmetric region size
98	    int     n_pes_;          // TP degree being simulated
99	    int     my_pe_;          // this CTA-group's virtual rank
100	
101	    __device__ __forceinline__ int my_pe() const { return my_pe_; }
102	    __device__ __forceinline__ int n_pes() const { return n_pes_; }
103	
104	    // THIS pe's buffer at symmetric offset `off`.
105	    __device__ __forceinline__ float* local(int64_t off) const {
106	        return heap_base + (int64_t)my_pe_ * stride_floats + off;
107	    }
108	    // Peer pe's buffer at the SAME symmetric offset (ascending-pe reads in the
109	    // fixed-order reduce). On NVSHMEM this is nvshmem_ptr(sym, pe); here it is
110	    // the strided region — same contract, swapped translation.
111	    __device__ __forceinline__ const float* peer(int64_t off, int pe) const {
112	        return heap_base + (int64_t)pe * stride_floats + off;
113	    }
114	
115	    // Cross-PE rendezvous. Loopback: every virtual PE lives in THIS grid, so the
116	    // whole-grid GridBarrier IS the cross-PE barrier (publish partials → sync →
117	    // read peers → sync → reuse slots).
118	    __device__ __forceinline__ void rendezvous(const ::sg::fused::GridBarrier& bar) const {
119	        bar.sync();
120	    }
121	
122	    // Static CTA→PE partition helper: contiguous CTA groups (CTA c of nCTA, P
123	    // pes → pe = c / (nCTA/P); caller guarantees nCTA % P == 0, asserted in the
124	    // launchers). Contiguity keeps each virtual rank's tile traversal identical
125	    // to a real per-GPU grid (ascending tiles within the rank).
126	    __host__ __device__ __forceinline__ static int pe_of_cta(int cta, int nCTA, int P) {
127	        return cta / (nCTA / P);
128	    }
129	    __host__ __device__ __forceinline__ static int cta_within_pe(int cta, int nCTA, int P) {
130	        return cta % (nCTA / P);
131	    }
132	    __host__ __device__ __forceinline__ static int ctas_per_pe(int nCTA, int P) {
133	        return nCTA / P;
134	    }
135	};
136	
137	#if defined(SG_HAS_NVSHMEM)
138	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
139	//  NvshmemTransport — the REAL device-initiated transport (design §5.2).
140	//  COMPILED ONLY under -DSG_HAS_NVSHMEM=1 (toolkit on the path). The math code
141	//  path is IDENTICAL to the loopback's; only the address translation + the
142	//  rendezvous scope differ:
143	//    * `heap_base` is an nvshmem_malloc'd SYMMETRIC allocation (same offset
144	//      valid on every PE);
145	//    * `peer()` translates via nvshmem_ptr (NVLink direct load/store — the
146	//      single-node 8×H100 case; a multi-node fabric would use nvshmem_get,
147	//      which is the documented extension point, NOT silently emulated);
148	//    * `rendezvous()` = in-GPU GridBarrier + ONE CTA running the cross-GPU
149	//      nvshmemx_barrier_all_block + GridBarrier again (so every CTA of every
150	//      GPU is fenced both sides — the §5.2 "two barrier systems must not
151	//      deadlock" discipline: the NVSHMEM barrier is entered by exactly one CTA
152	//      per GPU, never concurrently with the GridBarrier spin).
153	//  GO/NO-GO (§5.4): parity vs host-NCCL TP, A/A/A, MFU, ZeRO-3/DP composition —
154	//  all 8×H100-window activities (design §7.5).
155	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
156	struct NvshmemTransport {
157	    float*  heap_base;       // nvshmem_malloc'd symmetric base (LOCAL pointer)
158	    int     n_pes_;          // TP group size  (nvshmem_n_pes() on the TP team)
159	    int     my_pe_;          // this GPU's pe  (nvshmem_my_pe())
160	
161	    __device__ __forceinline__ int my_pe() const { return my_pe_; }
162	    __device__ __forceinline__ int n_pes() const { return n_pes_; }
163	
164	    __device__ __forceinline__ float* local(int64_t off) const {
165	        return heap_base + off;
166	    }
167	    __device__ __forceinline__ const float* peer(int64_t off, int pe) const {
168	        // NVLink path: direct load/store through the peer mapping. nvshmem_ptr
169	        // returns nullptr for non-P2P-reachable peers — single-node 8×H100 is
170	        // always reachable; the multi-node fall-back (nvshmem_get staging) is
171	        // future work and must NOT be silently approximated here.
172	        return static_cast<const float*>(nvshmem_ptr(heap_base, pe)) + off;
173	    }
174	
175	    __device__ __forceinline__ void rendezvous(const ::sg::fused::GridBarrier& bar) const {
176	        bar.sync();                       // all CTAs of THIS GPU arrived
177	        if (blockIdx.x == 0) {            // one CTA crosses the GPU boundary
178	            nvshmemx_barrier_all_block();
179	        }
180	        bar.sync();                       // release every CTA after the cross-GPU join
181	    }
182	};
183	#endif  // SG_HAS_NVSHMEM
184	
185	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
186	//  tp_allreduce_sum_fixed_order — THE all-reduce both transports share.
187	//
188	//  PRE: every PE has PUBLISHED its fp32 partial at symmetric offset `slot_off`
189	//  (length n) and the caller has crossed `tr.rendezvous(bar)` once (so all
190	//  publishes are visible). POST: `dst[i] = Σ_pe partial_pe[i]`, summed in
191	//  ASCENDING pe order in fp32 — bit-identical on every PE and across reruns
192	//  (design §5.2/§2.7: structural order, the A/A/A non-negotiable). The caller
193	//  crosses `tr.rendezvous(bar)` again before REUSING the slot.
194	//
195	//  `tid`/`nthreads` define this PE's cooperative element loop. In the loopback
196	//  every virtual PE redundantly computes its own copy (each PE strides its own
197	//  CTA group's threads) — exactly what real per-GPU ranks do.
198	//
199	//  This is deliberately NOT nvshmem_float_sum_reduce: that collective's
200	//  reduction order is unspecified ⇒ ULP drift run-to-run ⇒ A/A/A failure
201	//  (design §5.2). The hand-rolled ascending-pe loop IS the deliverable.
202	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
203	template <class Transport>
204	__device__ __forceinline__ void tp_allreduce_sum_fixed_order(
205	        const Transport& tr, int64_t slot_off, float* __restrict__ dst,
206	        int64_t n, int tid, int nthreads) {
207	    const int P = tr.n_pes();
208	    for (int64_t i = tid; i < n; i += nthreads) {
209	        float acc = 0.0f;
210	        #pragma unroll 1
211	        for (int pe = 0; pe < P; ++pe) {        // ASCENDING pe — fixed order
212	            acc += tr.peer(slot_off, pe)[i];
213	        }
214	        dst[i] = acc;
215	    }
216	}
217	
218	// Variant writing the reduced value back INTO this PE's symmetric slot (in-place
219	// consumers); same fixed order. Safe because every PE reads ALL peers before any
220	// PE can pass the post-reduce rendezvous the caller crosses before reuse — the
221	// read-before-overwrite hazard is what that second rendezvous exists for, so
222	// this variant must write to a DIFFERENT slot than it reads. Kept explicit:
223	template <class Transport>
224	__device__ __forceinline__ void tp_allreduce_sum_fixed_order_to_slot(
225	        const Transport& tr, int64_t src_slot_off, int64_t dst_slot_off,
226	        int64_t n, int tid, int nthreads) {
227	    float* dst = tr.local(dst_slot_off);
228	    tp_allreduce_sum_fixed_order(tr, src_slot_off, dst, n, tid, nthreads);
229	}

4	// csrc/fused/sm_90/sharded_optimizer_kernel.cuh — the POST-reduce-scatter
5	// sharded optimizer kernel for the ZeRO-2/3 multi-GPU step.
6	//
7	// IMPLEMENTS: /workspace/.parallelism_design.md §2.3 (the new, small sharded-
8	// optimizer kernel) — the second half of the owner's B2-seam decomposition
9	// (design §0.1/§2.1):
10	//     [fwd+bwd megakernel] → reduce-scatter(grad) → [THIS kernel] → all-gather(params)
11	//
12	// WHAT IT IS: under ZeRO>=2 the fused megakernel early-exits right after the B2
13	// barrier (design §2.2, `if constexpr (Par::kShardOptGrad) return;`) with the
14	// reduced LOCAL grad assembled. The host then reduce-scatters that grad so each
15	// rank holds the reduced grad for ONLY its owned shard. THIS kernel applies the
16	// optimizer over that owned shard. For the ELEMENTWISE optimizers it is exactly
17	// P3 (the fused tail) with the work-steal-over-30-tensors loop replaced by a
18	// flat grid-stride over [0, shard_numel) and NO GridBarrier (single phase).
19	//
20	// ZERO NEW MATH (design §2.3, the parity guarantee): every per-element update is
21	// the EXACT SAME `apply_optimizer<Opt>` from opt_components.cuh — the canonical
22	// `csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h` device math the in-kernel P3 tail already calls and
23	// the parity gates already validate. This file INCLUDES opt_components.cuh and
24	// reuses it verbatim; it does NOT edit it and adds no new optimizer math, so the
25	// sharded path inherits the single-GPU A/A/A correctness per element (design
26	// §7.3: the DP=1 sharded kernel must be bit-identical to the in-kernel P3).
27	//
28	// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
29	//  THE PER-TENSOR BOUNDARY (design §2.3 / §3.4 / §0.4) — read before using this
30	//  for muon / SuperGrok11 / SuperGrok15 / SuperGrok2:
31	//
32	//  `apply_optimizer<Opt>` is, for ALL 11 OptIds, a PURELY ELEMENTWISE update of
33	//  one `idx`: it consumes ONLY per-element state (exp_avg/exp_avg_sq/ema/...) and
34	//  PRE-COMPUTED inputs carried in FusedOptState (st.orth, st.mu, st.gate,
35	//  st.smart_grad, st.sam_dir, st.d_factor, st.clip_coef, ...). So this flat
36	//  grid-stride kernel COMPILES and RUNS correctly for any OptId *whose
37	//  FusedOptState inputs are already filled* — i.e. it is a complete, correct
38	//  optimizer step for:
39	//
40	//    ELEMENTWISE-DRIVABLE (this kernel alone is sufficient at DP):
41	//      adamw(0), lion(1), grokfast(2), neuralgrok(6),
42	//      and the ELEMENTWISE CORE of grokadamw(3)/looksam(4)/prodigy(5)
43	//      *given* their global/precomputed scalar already in st (clip_coef /
44	//      sam_dir / d_factor — see the next paragraph for where those come from).
45	//
46	//    PER-TENSOR / PER-MATRIX (this kernel is the APPLY ONLY — its st inputs need
47	//    an UPSTREAM stage that is OUT OF SCOPE for this kernel):
48	//      muon(7)        → st.orth     : Newton–Schulz over a WHOLE 2D weight (P2.7)
49	//      supergrok11(8) → st.mu/gate  : per-TENSOR meta-net mu/gate (P2.45)
50	//      supergrok15(9) → st.mu/gate  : per-TENSOR meta-net mu     (P2.45)
51	//      supergrok2(10) → st.smart_grad: per-TENSOR CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU + segmented
52	//                                      sort meta-net (STAGE -1 + P3-SG2)
53	//    Those P2.x stages cooperate across CTAs PER matrix/tensor on the GridBarrier
54	//    substrate, so they REQUIRE the tensor whole on one rank — which forces the
55	//    ZeRO-3 shard to be TENSOR-GRANULAR for these cells (design §3.4;
56	//    grokking_optimizers/parallel/shard_map.py::partition_tensor_granular). The
57	//    sharded-optimizer kernel FOR THEM is the *full* persistent megakernel
58	//    restricted to the tensors this rank owns (design §2.3) — NOT this flat
59	//    kernel. This flat kernel deliberately does NOT run those P2.x stages; it
60	//    only does the elementwise apply once their st inputs exist.
61	//
62	//  Likewise the GLOBAL-scalar cells (prodigy d, grokadamw grad-norm clip_coef,
63	//  looksam ‖g‖) need a cross-DP all-reduce of one/two scalars BEFORE this kernel
64	//  (design §2.4) so every rank's `st.d_factor`/`st.clip_coef` agree; that
65	//  all-reduce is host-side orchestration (design §6.2 step 4), also out of scope
66	//  here. This kernel just consumes the agreed scalar from st.
67	//
68	//  Net: every OptId COMPILE-CHECKS here (apply_optimizer is elementwise). Which
69	//  ones are *correct from this kernel alone* vs need the upstream stage/all-
70	//  reduce is the taxonomy above — documented per design §2.3/§3.4, enforced by
71	//  the host shard-mode selection (elementwise → flat-even; per-tensor →
72	//  tensor-granular).
73	// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
74	//
75	// CPU/1-GPU AUTHORABLE (design §7.3): this is the cut the test_sharded_optimizer
76	// gate validates entirely on one GPU. Authored here as NEW code; the kernel
77	// builder owns wiring it into dispatch + the explicit instantiations.

81	#include <cuda_runtime.h>

83	// The canonical per-optimizer elementwise math + the FusedOptState ABI. We REUSE
84	// apply_optimizer<Opt> / OptId / FusedOptState verbatim — INCLUDE, do not edit
85	// (design §2.3: zero new math, reuse the validated single-GPU tail).
86	#include "csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh"

90	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
91	//  sharded_optimizer_kernel<Opt, Par> — flat grid-stride over the OWNED shard.
92	//
93	//  Args (design §2.3 signature):
94	//    params_shard : [shard_numel] this rank's owned param slice (mutated in place)
95	//    grad_shard   : [shard_numel] the reduce-scattered grad for the owned slice
96	//    lr, step     : the step's learning rate + 1-based step counter
97	//    st_shard     : FusedOptState whose pointers are ALREADY rebased to the shard
98	//                   (the host offsets exp_avg/exp_avg_sq/ema/... to the owned
99	//                   slice before launch — the per-element ABI is shard-local, so
100	//                   index `i` into params_shard pairs with index `i` into every
101	//                   st_shard buffer, exactly like the in-kernel P3 owns each
102	//                   element once). st_shard also carries the per-step scalars
103	//                   already folded via apply_scalars (bc1/bc2/d_factor/clip_coef/
104	//                   gate/...), and the precomputed per-tensor pointers (orth/mu/
105	//                   smart_grad/sam_dir) for the per-tensor cells.
106	//
107	//  NO GridBarrier (single phase): the work-steal-over-30-tensors loop of P3 is
108	//  replaced by one flat grid-stride over [0, shard_numel). Each element is
109	//  written exactly once by the thread that owns its `i`, so there is no cross-CTA
110	//  dependence and no barrier (design §2.3). `lr` is threaded into st_shard.lr so
111	//  apply_optimizer reads a single source for the rate (matches the P3 contract).
112	//
113	//  Par is carried for ABI/symmetry with the megakernel template (design §1.1)
114	//  and to let a builder add `if constexpr (Par::kEmitComm)` hooks later (e.g. a
115	//  fused all-gather-on-write for ZeRO-3). It is otherwise unused by the
116	//  elementwise apply — the shard is already local when this kernel runs.
117	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
118	template <OptId Opt, class Par>
119	__global__ void sharded_optimizer_kernel(
120	        float* __restrict__ params_shard,        // [shard_numel] owned param slice
121	        const float* __restrict__ grad_shard,    // [shard_numel] reduce-scattered grad
122	        int64_t shard_numel,
123	        float lr, int step,
124	        FusedOptState st_shard /* pointers pre-rebased to the shard */) {
125	    // Single source for the rate (the P3 tail reads st.lr; mirror that here so a
126	    // caller that passes lr positionally and a caller that pre-folds it via
127	    // apply_scalars agree bit-for-bit).
128	    st_shard.lr = lr;
129	
130	    const int64_t stride = static_cast<int64_t>(blockDim.x) * gridDim.x;
131	    int64_t i = static_cast<int64_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
132	    for (; i < shard_numel; i += stride) {
133	        // EXACT same canonical math as the in-kernel P3 tail (opt_components.cuh).
134	        // Shard-local index i pairs params_shard[i] with grad_shard[i] and every
135	        // pre-rebased st_shard buffer at [i]. Zero new math (design §2.3).
136	        apply_optimizer<Opt>(params_shard, grad_shard, i, step, st_shard);
137	    }
138	}

140	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
141	//  Host launcher — a thin grid-stride launch (design §2.3: "~30 lines, no
142	//  GridBarrier, single phase"). Sized to the shard, NOT the full param set. A
143	//  kernel builder routes this from dispatch behind the ZeRO>=2 path + the
144	//  explicit ParConfig instantiation allow-list (design §1.3/§7.2); it is left
145	//  here as the canonical small launcher so the kernel has a tested entry point.
146	//
147	//  NOTE: no GPU is launched in this CPU/1-GPU pre-work (design §7); this launcher
148	//  is COMPILE-CHECKED only. block=256 mirrors the per-op elementwise launchers'
149	//  default; grid is capped so the grid-stride covers any shard_numel.
150	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
151	template <OptId Opt, class Par>
152	inline cudaError_t launch_sharded_optimizer_kernel(
153	        float* params_shard, const float* grad_shard, int64_t shard_numel,
154	        float lr, int step, const FusedOptState& st_shard,
155	        cudaStream_t stream = nullptr, int block = 256, int max_grid = 65535) {
156	    if (shard_numel <= 0) return cudaSuccess;
157	    int64_t want = (shard_numel + block - 1) / block;
158	    int grid = static_cast<int>(want < max_grid ? want : max_grid);
159	    if (grid < 1) grid = 1;
160	    sharded_optimizer_kernel<Opt, Par><<<grid, block, 0, stream>>>(
161	        params_shard, grad_shard, shard_numel, lr, step, st_shard);
162	    return cudaGetLastError();
163	}

44	// bigger workspace). Zeroed in-kernel (P0) each launch; never freed (one per
45	// device, leaked at process exit like every other cuBLAS/cuDNN handle).
46	struct DecTcLauncherScratch {
47	    int*     g_next = nullptr;        // int [1]
48	    unsigned* g_arrived = nullptr;    // unsigned [1]
49	    unsigned* g_generation = nullptr; // unsigned [1]
50	    float*   workspace = nullptr;     // float [dec_tc_workspace_floats(T,B,nCTA)]
51	    int64_t  ws_floats = 0;
52	    int      dev = -1;
53	};
54	
55	DecTcLauncherScratch& dec_tc_launcher_scratch(int dev, int64_t need_floats) {
56	    static DecTcLauncherScratch s;
57	    if (s.dev != dev) {
58	        // First use on this device (or a device switch — the race is single-GPU,
59	        // but be honest if it ever moves): (re)allocate the counters.
60	        s.dev = dev;
61	        if (!s.g_next)      cudaMalloc(&s.g_next, sizeof(int));
62	        if (!s.g_arrived)   cudaMalloc(&s.g_arrived, sizeof(unsigned));
63	        if (!s.g_generation)cudaMalloc(&s.g_generation, sizeof(unsigned));
64	    }
65	    if (s.ws_floats < need_floats) {
66	        if (s.workspace) cudaFree(s.workspace);
67	        cudaMalloc(&s.workspace, (size_t)need_floats * sizeof(float));
68	        s.ws_floats = need_floats;
69	    }
70	    return s;
71	}

74	// mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc — the WIRED TC launcher. Boundary mirrors the scalar
75	// mega_decoder_real_adamw (dispatch.cpp extern-decls it with the same mirror
76	// types) EXCEPT it takes NO workspace pointer: the TC workspace is a different
77	// size from the scalar nCTA*total partials, so this TU allocates+owns it. `loss_out`
78	// still points into the caller's state[3*total] slot (dispatch reads it back).
79	//
80	// OPTID-GENERIC (owner baseline directive — all 33 cells on L3-TC): the fwd+bwd+
81	// grad-reduction is OPTIMIZER-INDEPENDENT (the same validated wgmma decoder kernel);
82	// ONLY the per-element optimizer TAIL (apply_optimizer<Opt>) differs, and that tail
83	// is the 14/0-apply-parity math already in opt_components.cuh. So this launcher
84	// takes `opt_id` (the OptId int) and dispatches to the matching kernel instantiation
85	// over the SAME state buffer. The state layout is [m | v | extra] (3*total) + loss:
86	//   * lion              uses m only (v/extra unread; bound harmlessly)
87	//   * adamw             uses m, v
88	//   * grokfast/grokadamw use m, v, ema  (ema == the `extra` slice, state + 2*total)
89	//   * neuralgrok        uses m, v, AND a psi-net weight pack the cell supplies in the
90	//                       `extra` slice (kPsiPackFloats floats); st.psi_W1/b1/W2 bind
91	//                       to those offsets, exactly as opt_components.cuh documents.
92	// The STAGED optimizers prodigy (P2.6 global-d) and muon (P2.7 grid-cooperative NS)
93	// ARE routed here: their precompute is an IN-KERNEL phase, so they remain a SINGLE
94	// persistent launch (the cases below). The SAM-coupled SG11/SG15/looksam and SG2 are
95	// NOT — they need a 2nd in-kernel fwd+bwd / a sharpness ABI field / a segmented sort
96	// that this single-launch path does not carry; dispatch.cpp gates them out (and
97	// wiring_check fails them loud with the cited reason). NeuralGrok is wired but its
98	// host-trained amplifier is a separate concern (the race fn gates it).
99	//
100	// ncta_cap: forwarded to the TC launcher (0 = one CTA/SM = full saturation, the
101	// shipped config). The race always passes 0.
102	cudaError_t mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc(
103	        PersistentContext ctx, float* params,
104	        const int* tokens, const int* targets, int B,
105	        float* state, float* grad, float* /*workspace_unused*/, float* loss_out,
106	        const int* sizes, const int* offsets,
107	        float lr, int step, const FusedScalars& scalars, cudaStream_t stream,
108	        int ncta_cap, int opt_id) {
109	    (void)sizes; (void)offsets;  // TC kernel reads kDecSizes/kDecOffsets directly.
110	
111	    const int64_t total = kDecTotalElems;
112	    const int T = B * dec::kSeq;
113	
114	    int dev = 0;
115	    cudaError_t err = cudaGetDevice(&dev);
116	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
117	    int n_sms = 1;
118	    err = cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&n_sms, cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount, dev);
119	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
120	    int nCTA = n_sms;
121	    if (ncta_cap > 0 && ncta_cap < nCTA) nCTA = ncta_cap;
122	
123	    const int64_t need = dec_tc_workspace_floats(T, B, nCTA);
124	    DecTcLauncherScratch& sc = dec_tc_launcher_scratch(dev, need);
125	
126	    // Re-point the ctx counters at THIS TU's cached counters (dispatch.cpp built
127	    // ctx pointing at its scalar DecoderScratch counters; the TC launcher zeroes
128	    // them per-launch, but they must be the ones this scratch owns so the grid
129	    // barrier is consistent with the workspace).
130	    ctx.g_next_task   = sc.g_next;
131	    ctx.g_arrived     = sc.g_arrived;
132	    ctx.g_generation  = sc.g_generation;
133	    ctx.n_tasks       = kDecNumTensors;  // parameter tensors for reduce+opt phases
134	
135	    // Bind the optimizer state slices. [m | v | extra] over the SAME state buffer;
136	    // each tail reads only its own buffers (opt_components.cuh guarantees unused
137	    // pointers are never dereferenced). ema/psi-net live in the `extra` slice.
138	    float* const m_slice     = state;
139	    float* const v_slice     = state + total;
140	    float* const extra_slice = state + 2 * total;
141	    FusedOptState st;
142	    st.exp_avg    = m_slice;
143	    st.exp_avg_sq = v_slice;
144	    st.ema        = extra_slice;          // grokfast/grokadamw slow-grad EMA
145	    // NeuralGrok psi-net pack (kPsiPackFloats floats at the head of `extra`): the
146	    // cell places [psi_W1 | psi_b1 | psi_W2 | psi_b2] there; bind the device pointers
147	    // so the apply reads real weights (psi_b2 is read on-device from psi_W2[kPsiHidden]).
148	    st.psi_W1     = extra_slice + kPsiW1Off;
149	    st.psi_b1     = extra_slice + kPsiB1Off;
150	    st.psi_W2     = extra_slice + kPsiW2Off;
151	    // PRODIGY (STAGED global-d) state bindings. The cell extends the state buffer
152	    // to [m | v | extra/s_track | loss | param_init | r_ema | s_ema | d_lr] (host
153	    // sizes it to >= 4*total + 4; see dispatch.fused_train_step). The `extra` slice
154	    // doubles as Prodigy's `s` trajectory accumulator (the apply reads st.s_track,
155	    // not st.ema — they alias here, harmless: Prodigy has no slow-grad EMA). The
156	    // trajectory anchor p0 (param_init) follows the loss slot; the 3 persisted
157	    // estimator scalars [r_ema | s_ema | d_lr] follow param_init. loss_out points at
158	    // state+3*total (dispatch's loss_slot), so param_init = loss_out + 1.
159	    st.s_track        = extra_slice;            // Prodigy `s` (per-element accumulator)
160	    st.param_init     = loss_out + 1;           // state + 3*total + 1
161	    st.prodigy_persist = loss_out + 1 + total;  // [r_ema | s_ema | d_lr]
162	    // LookSAM (MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward): sam_dir is the PERSISTENT cached SAM
163	    // direction (g_sam − g), carried across steps in the `extra` slice (aliases the
164	    // grokfast EMA / Prodigy s_track slot — harmless: LookSAM has none of those). The
165	    // in-kernel P2.4 phase WRITES it on SAM steps; the apply tail READS it every step.
166	    st.sam_dir        = extra_slice;            // [total] cached SAM direction
167	    // SuperGrok11/15 (MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward + per-tensor meta-net mu). State
168	    // layout: [m | v | mu | loss | sharpness(total) | phi_pack(4H+1)].
169	    //   * st.mu = the `extra` slice (recomputed each step by the P2.45 precompute; the
170	    //     apply reads it — it aliases sam_dir/ema/s_track, harmless: SG has none).
171	    //   * st.sharpness = loss_slot+1 (PERSISTED (g_sam−g)²; the P2.4 SAM 2nd backward
172	    //     writes it on SAM steps, the cached value is reused on intervening steps).
173	    //   * st.sg_phi_W1/b1/W2 = the phi pack at sharpness+total (host-scattered each step,
174	    //     like NeuralGrok's psi pack); sg_phi_b2 is read on-device from sg_phi_W2[H].
175	    st.mu             = extra_slice;            // [total] meta-net mu (P2.45-filled)
176	    {
177	        float* sharp_base = loss_out + 1;       // state + 3*total + 1
178	        float* phi_base   = sharp_base + total; // phi pack after sharpness
179	        st.sharpness = sharp_base;
180	        st.sg_phi_W1 = phi_base + kSgPhiW1Off;
181	        st.sg_phi_b1 = phi_base + kSgPhiB1Off;
182	        st.sg_phi_W2 = phi_base + kSgPhiW2Off;  // sg_phi_b2 read on-device from [H]
183	    }
184	    apply_scalars(st, scalars);   // FULL scalar set (un-frozen bc1/bc2/... + d0/d_coef/beta3 + rho/looksam_sam/sg_rescale)
185	    st.lr = lr;
186	
187	    DecoderTokenCtx tok;
188	    tok.tokens    = tokens;
189	    tok.targets   = targets;
190	    tok.B         = B;
191	    tok.workspace = sc.workspace;
192	    tok.loss_out  = loss_out;
193	
194	    // Dispatch to the matching kernel instantiation. The fwd+bwd is identical across
195	    // these OptIds; the template differs ONLY in the P3 apply_optimizer<Opt> tail.
196	    // Unsupported opt_ids return cudaErrorInvalidValue → dispatch.cpp throws LOUD (no
197	    // silent scalar/adamw fallback — the no-suppression rule). The STAGED/model-coupled
198	    // optimizers are intentionally NOT cases here (they cannot run as a single launch).
199	    switch (static_cast<OptId>(opt_id)) {
200	        case OptId::AdamW:
201	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::AdamW>(
202	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
203	        case OptId::Lion:
204	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::Lion>(
205	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
206	        case OptId::Grokfast:
207	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::Grokfast>(
208	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
209	        case OptId::GrokAdamW:
210	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::GrokAdamW>(
211	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
212	        case OptId::NeuralGrok:
213	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::NeuralGrok>(
214	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
215	        case OptId::Prodigy:
216	            // STAGED global-d: the SAME single persistent launch — the d-estimate
217	            // cross-tensor reduction is an IN-KERNEL phase (P2.6, between B2 and P3),
218	            // not a separate launch. st carries param_init/prodigy_persist/d0/d_coef/
219	            // beta3; the kernel decays+accumulates the EMA, updates d, applies.
220	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::Prodigy>(
221	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
222	        case OptId::Muon:
223	            // STAGED grid-cooperative Newton-Schulz (wave-2 decoder lane): the SAME
224	            // single persistent launch — the NS orthogonalization of the 11 2D weights
225	            // (tok/pos/in_proj/out_proj/ff.0/ff.2/out) is an IN-KERNEL phase (P2.7,
226	            // between B2/P2.6 and P3), grid-barrier-looped per matrix, NOT a separate
227	            // launch. The per-matrix NS scratch lives in the workspace (dec_tc_muon_floats,
228	            // carved after the Prodigy reduce slots). The persistent momentum buffer is
229	            // the m-slice (st.exp_avg); the 1D/non-2D weights take the AdamW tail in P3
230	            // reading the INDEPENDENT aux_lr/aux_betas (eager Muon adamw_* group). The
231	            // vit twin (mega_vit_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu) proved this routing.
232	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::Muon>(
233	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
234	        case OptId::LookSAM:
235	            // MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward (wave-2 decoder lane): the SAME single
236	            // persistent launch — the perturb→2nd in-kernel fwd+bwd→sam_dir=g_sam−g is
237	            // an IN-KERNEL phase (P2.4, between B2 and P2.5/P3), gated to every-k SAM
238	            // steps by st.looksam_sam. The transient backup + g_sam buffers live in the
239	            // workspace (dec_tc_looksam_floats, carved after the Muon scratch); sam_dir
240	            // persists in the extra slice (st.sam_dir, bound above). The apply tail (P3)
241	            // blends g_adj=(1−α)g+α·sam_dir and runs AdamW. NOT a separate launch.
242	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::LookSAM>(
243	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
244	        case OptId::SuperGrok11:
245	            // MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward + per-tensor meta-net mu/gate (wave-3
246	            // decoder lane): the SAME single persistent launch. The SAM 2nd backward
247	            // (P2.4, sharpness=(g_sam−g)²) + the per-tensor mu precompute (P2.45,
248	            // mu=rescale·phi(g,sharpness)) + the per-tensor cosine gate are ALL
249	            // in-kernel phases between B2 and P3; the apply tail (sg11_sweep_b_step:
250	            // smart_grad=g+(1−gate)·alpha·mu, AdamW) runs in P3. The SAM scratch reuses
251	            // the looksam buffers (dec_tc_looksam_floats); sharpness + the phi pack ride
252	            // the extended state buffer (bound above). NOT a separate launch.
253	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::SuperGrok11>(
254	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
255	        case OptId::SuperGrok15:
256	            // Same SAM 2nd backward + mu precompute as SG11, but SIMPLER tail: the gate
257	            // is a host scalar (st.gate = sigmoid(accuracy)), NO per-tensor cosine stage;
258	            // the apply tail (sg15_sweep_b_step) does the per-coord alpha clip + smart_grad
259	            // = g + gate·a·mu + AdamW. Single persistent launch.
260	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::SuperGrok15>(
261	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
262	        default:
263	            return cudaErrorInvalidValue;  // STAGED/coupled opt not single-launch TC
264	    }

267	// mega_decoder_sg2_tc — the DEDICATED SuperGrok2 TC launcher. SG2 needs the FULL
268	// CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU meta-net weight bundle (26 HBM pointers, model-independent) +
269	// per-tensor scalar ARRAYS (alpha/gru_decay/lamb_eff/beta1/bc1/bc2, length P) +
270	// the meta-net state (m/v/mu/slow/gru_state/sharpness), none of which fit the
271	// FusedScalars POD or the generic mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc boundary. So this is
272	// a PARALLEL entry (the generic launcher + the 28 byte-identical cells are
273	// UNTOUCHED). It binds the SG2 state slices, threads the weight bundle + scalar
274	// arrays through FusedOptState's sg2_* fields, and dispatches the OptId::SuperGrok2
275	// kernel instantiation (its P3-SG2 phase runs sg2_meta_stages per tensor: STAGE -1
276	// in-kernel segmented sort → CSA/HCA/GRU/PEER/apply, reading st.sharpness from the
277	// SAM 2nd backward (P2.4, shared with SG11/15)).
278	//
279	// STATE LAYOUT (host sizes it; this carves it):
280	//   [m(total) | v(total) | mu(total) | loss(1) | sharpness(total) | slow(total)
281	//    | gru_state(total*GH)]   ⇒ min_state = (4+1+GH)*total + 1   (GH=gru_hidden=4)
282	// perm/unsort are built IN-KERNEL into the per-CTA workspace (NOT state).
283	cudaError_t mega_decoder_sg2_tc(
284	        PersistentContext ctx, float* params,
285	        const int* tokens, const int* targets, int B,
286	        float* state, float* grad, float* loss_out,
287	        // SG2 meta-net weight bundle (HBM, fp32, model-independent), in SG2Weights order.
288	        const float* input_proj_W, const float* input_proj_b,
289	        const float* csa_q_W, const float* csa_k_W, const float* csa_v_W, const float* csa_out_W,
290	        const float* csa_compress_w, const float* csa_idx_DQ, const float* csa_idx_K,
291	        const float* hca_q_W, const float* hca_k_W, const float* hca_v_W, const float* hca_out_W,
292	        const float* gru_Wz, const float* gru_bz, const float* gru_Wr, const float* gru_br,
293	        const float* gru_Wh, const float* gru_bh,
294	        const float* peer_query_Ws, const float* prod_keys_A, const float* prod_keys_B,
295	        const float* expert_W1, const float* expert_b1, const float* expert_W2, const float* expert_b2,
296	        // per-tensor scalar arrays (device, length kDecNumTensors).
297	        const float* sc_alpha, const float* sc_gru_decay, const float* sc_lamb_eff,
298	        const float* sc_beta1, const float* sc_bc1, const float* sc_bc2,
299	        // shared scalars + the SAM 2nd-backward gate (SG2 reuses the LookSAM P2.4
300	        // machinery: rho = perturbation radius, sam_on = every-k SAM-step gate).
301	        float rescale, float beta2, float lr, float wd, float eps,
302	        float rho, float sam_on,
303	        int step, cudaStream_t stream, int ncta_cap) {
304	    const int64_t total = kDecTotalElems;
305	    // gru_state spans total*GH (GH=DecSG2Dims::gru_hidden); the layout is fixed by
306	    // the kernel's SG2State carve, so the slices below need no GH arithmetic here.
307	    const int T = B * dec::kSeq;
308	
309	    int dev = 0;
310	    cudaError_t err = cudaGetDevice(&dev);
311	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
312	    int n_sms = 1;
313	    err = cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&n_sms, cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount, dev);
314	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
315	    int nCTA = n_sms;
316	    if (ncta_cap > 0 && ncta_cap < nCTA) nCTA = ncta_cap;
317	
318	    const int64_t need = dec_tc_workspace_floats(T, B, nCTA);
319	    DecTcLauncherScratch& sc = dec_tc_launcher_scratch(dev, need);
320	    ctx.g_next_task   = sc.g_next;
321	    ctx.g_arrived     = sc.g_arrived;
322	    ctx.g_generation  = sc.g_generation;
323	    ctx.n_tasks       = kDecNumTensors;
324	
325	    // Bind the SG2 state slices: [m | v | mu | loss | sharpness | slow | gru_state].
326	    FusedOptState st;
327	    st.exp_avg     = state;                       // m
328	    st.exp_avg_sq  = state + total;               // v
329	    st.mu          = state + 2 * total;           // expert-output EMA
330	    // loss_out points at state + 3*total (dispatch's loss slot).
331	    float* sharp_base = loss_out + 1;             // state + 3*total + 1
332	    st.sharpness   = sharp_base;                  // (g_sam − g)² (SAM 2nd backward, P2.4)
333	    st.sg2_slow    = sharp_base + total;          // grokfast slow-grad EMA
334	    st.sg2_gru_state = st.sg2_slow + total;       // [total*GH] per-element GRU state
335	    // meta-net weight bundle (HBM).
336	    st.sg2_input_proj_W = input_proj_W; st.sg2_input_proj_b = input_proj_b;
337	    st.sg2_csa_q_W = csa_q_W; st.sg2_csa_k_W = csa_k_W; st.sg2_csa_v_W = csa_v_W;
338	    st.sg2_csa_out_W = csa_out_W; st.sg2_csa_compress_w = csa_compress_w;
339	    st.sg2_csa_idx_DQ = csa_idx_DQ; st.sg2_csa_idx_K = csa_idx_K;
340	    st.sg2_hca_q_W = hca_q_W; st.sg2_hca_k_W = hca_k_W; st.sg2_hca_v_W = hca_v_W;
341	    st.sg2_hca_out_W = hca_out_W;
342	    st.sg2_gru_Wz = gru_Wz; st.sg2_gru_bz = gru_bz; st.sg2_gru_Wr = gru_Wr;
343	    st.sg2_gru_br = gru_br; st.sg2_gru_Wh = gru_Wh; st.sg2_gru_bh = gru_bh;
344	    st.sg2_peer_query_Ws = peer_query_Ws; st.sg2_prod_keys_A = prod_keys_A;
345	    st.sg2_prod_keys_B = prod_keys_B;
346	    st.sg2_expert_W1 = expert_W1; st.sg2_expert_b1 = expert_b1;
347	    st.sg2_expert_W2 = expert_W2; st.sg2_expert_b2 = expert_b2;
348	    // per-tensor scalar arrays.
349	    st.sg2_alpha = sc_alpha; st.sg2_gru_decay = sc_gru_decay; st.sg2_lamb_eff = sc_lamb_eff;
350	    st.sg2_beta1 = sc_beta1; st.sg2_bc1 = sc_bc1; st.sg2_bc2 = sc_bc2;
351	    st.sg2_rescale = rescale;
352	    // shared scalars the SG2 phase reads (beta2/lr/wd/eps via FusedScalars fields).
353	    st.beta2 = beta2; st.lr = lr; st.wd = wd; st.eps = eps;
354	    // SAM 2nd-backward gate: SG2 reuses the LookSAM P2.4 machinery. st.rho is the
355	    // perturbation radius (SG2's sam_rho); st.looksam_sam is the every-k SAM-step gate
356	    // (1.0 ⇒ run the in-kernel perturb→2nd fwd+bwd→sharpness=(g_sam−g)² this step;
357	    // 0.0 ⇒ reuse the cached sharpness). On a non-SAM step the cached sharpness feeds
358	    // the meta-net verbatim (eager-faithful).
359	    st.rho = rho;
360	    st.looksam_sam = sam_on;
361	
362	    DecoderTokenCtx tok;
363	    tok.tokens    = tokens;
364	    tok.targets   = targets;
365	    tok.B         = B;
366	    tok.workspace = sc.workspace;
367	    tok.loss_out  = loss_out;
368	
369	    return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::SuperGrok2>(
370	        ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
371	}

60	struct MbTcLauncherScratch {
61	    int*      g_next = nullptr;        // int [1]
62	    unsigned* g_arrived = nullptr;     // unsigned [1]
63	    unsigned* g_generation = nullptr;  // unsigned [1]
64	    float*    workspace = nullptr;     // float [mb_tc_workspace_floats(T, nCTA)]

69	MbTcLauncherScratch& mb_tc_launcher_scratch(int dev, int64_t need_floats) {
70	    static MbTcLauncherScratch s;
71	    if (s.dev != dev) {
72	        s.dev = dev;
73	        if (!s.g_next)       cudaMalloc(&s.g_next, sizeof(int));
74	        if (!s.g_arrived)    cudaMalloc(&s.g_arrived, sizeof(unsigned));
75	        if (!s.g_generation) cudaMalloc(&s.g_generation, sizeof(unsigned));
76	    }
77	    if (s.ws_floats < need_floats) {
78	        if (s.workspace) cudaFree(s.workspace);
79	        cudaMalloc(&s.workspace, (size_t)need_floats * sizeof(float));
80	        s.ws_floats = need_floats;
81	    }
82	    return s;
83	}

86	// mega_mamba_real_adamw_tc — the WIRED Mamba TC launcher. Boundary mirrors the scalar
87	// mega_mamba_real_adamw (dispatch.cpp extern-decls it with the same mirror types)
88	// EXCEPT it takes NO workspace pointer: the TC workspace is a different size from the
89	// scalar partials, so this TU allocates+owns it. `loss_out` still points into the
90	// caller's state[3*total] slot (dispatch reads it back). `opt_id` selects the tail.
91	//
92	// ncta_cap: forwarded to the TC launcher (0 = one CTA/SM = full saturation, the
93	// shipped config). The race always passes 0.
94	cudaError_t mega_mamba_real_adamw_tc(
95	        PersistentContext ctx, float* params,
96	        const int* tokens, const int* targets, int B,
97	        float* state, float* grad, float* /*workspace_unused*/, float* loss_out,
98	        float lr, int step, const FusedScalars& scalars, cudaStream_t stream,
99	        int ncta_cap, int opt_id) {
100	    const int64_t total = kMambaTotalElems;
101	    const int T = B * mb::kSeq;
102	
103	    int dev = 0;
104	    cudaError_t err = cudaGetDevice(&dev);
105	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
106	    int n_sms = 1;
107	    err = cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&n_sms, cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount, dev);
108	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
109	    // Size the workspace for the EXACT count the kernel launcher runs (occ·n_sms with
110	    // the occupancy-fill default; reg-capped uniform across OptIds, so AdamW's count
111	    // == every tail's). Falls back to n_sms if the occ query fails.
112	    int nCTA = mb_tc_launched_nctas<OptId::AdamW>(dev, ncta_cap);
113	    if (nCTA <= 0) { nCTA = n_sms; if (ncta_cap > 0 && ncta_cap < nCTA) nCTA = ncta_cap; }
114	
115	    const int64_t need = mb_tc_workspace_floats(T, nCTA);
116	    MbTcLauncherScratch& sc = mb_tc_launcher_scratch(dev, need);
117	
118	    // Re-point the ctx counters at THIS TU's cached counters (the TC launcher zeroes
119	    // them per-launch, but they must be the ones this scratch owns so the grid
120	    // barrier is consistent with the workspace).
121	    ctx.g_next_task  = sc.g_next;
122	    ctx.g_arrived    = sc.g_arrived;
123	    ctx.g_generation = sc.g_generation;
124	    ctx.n_tasks      = kMambaNumTensors;   // parameter tensors for reduce+opt phases
125	
126	    // Bind the optimizer state slices. [m | v | extra] over the SAME state buffer;
127	    // each tail reads only its own buffers (opt_components.cuh guarantees unused
128	    // pointers are never dereferenced). ema/psi-net live in the `extra` slice.
129	    float* const extra_slice = state + 2 * total;
130	    FusedOptState st;
131	    st.exp_avg    = state;
132	    st.exp_avg_sq = state + total;
133	    st.ema        = extra_slice;          // grokfast/grokadamw slow-grad EMA
134	    st.psi_W1     = extra_slice + kPsiW1Off;   // neuralgrok psi-net pack (when wired)
135	    st.psi_b1     = extra_slice + kPsiB1Off;
136	    st.psi_W2     = extra_slice + kPsiW2Off;
137	    // PRODIGY (STAGED global-d) state bindings (mirror the decoder/vit TC launchers).
138	    // The cell extends the state buffer to [m | v | extra/s_track | loss | param_init |
139	    // r_ema | s_ema | d_lr] (host sizes it >= 4*total+4; dispatch.fused_train_step). The
140	    // `extra` slice doubles as Prodigy's `s` trajectory accumulator (the apply reads
141	    // st.s_track, not st.ema — they alias here, harmless: Prodigy has no slow-grad EMA).
142	    // loss_out == dispatch's loss_slot (state+3*total), so param_init = loss_out+1 and
143	    // the 3 persisted estimator scalars [r_ema | s_ema | d_lr] follow param_init.
144	    st.s_track        = extra_slice;            // Prodigy `s` (per-element accumulator)
145	    st.param_init     = loss_out + 1;           // state + 3*total + 1
146	    st.prodigy_persist = loss_out + 1 + total;  // [r_ema | s_ema | d_lr]
147	    // LookSAM (MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward) — the Mamba twin of the decoder/vit TC
148	    // launchers' sam_dir binding. sam_dir is the PERSISTENT cached SAM direction
149	    // (g_sam − g), carried across steps in the `extra` slice (aliases the grokfast EMA /
150	    // Prodigy s_track slot — harmless: LookSAM has none of those). The in-kernel P2.4
151	    // phase WRITES it on SAM steps (st.looksam_sam!=0); the apply tail READS it every step.
152	    st.sam_dir        = extra_slice;            // [total] cached SAM direction
153	    // SuperGrok11/15 (MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward + per-tensor meta-net mu) — the
154	    // mamba twin of the decoder/vit TC launchers. State layout:
155	    //   [m | v | mu | loss | sharpness(total) | phi_pack(4H+1)].
156	    //   * st.mu = the `extra` slice (recomputed each step by the P2.45/P3 precompute; the
157	    //     apply reads it — it aliases sam_dir/ema/s_track, harmless: SG has none).
158	    //   * st.sharpness = loss_slot+1 (PERSISTED (g_sam−g)²; the P2.4 SAM 2nd backward
159	    //     writes it on SAM steps, the cached value is reused on intervening steps).
160	    //   * st.sg_phi_W1/b1/W2 = the phi pack at sharpness+total (host-scattered each step,
161	    //     like NeuralGrok's psi pack); sg_phi_b2 read on-device from sg_phi_W2[H].
162	    st.mu             = extra_slice;            // [total] meta-net mu (P2.45/P3-filled)
163	    {
164	        float* sharp_base = loss_out + 1;       // state + 3*total + 1
165	        float* phi_base   = sharp_base + total; // phi pack after sharpness
166	        st.sharpness = sharp_base;
167	        st.sg_phi_W1 = phi_base + kSgPhiW1Off;
168	        st.sg_phi_b1 = phi_base + kSgPhiB1Off;
169	        st.sg_phi_W2 = phi_base + kSgPhiW2Off;  // sg_phi_b2 read on-device from [H]
170	    }
171	    apply_scalars(st, scalars);   // FULL scalar set (un-frozen bc1/bc2/... + d0/d_coef/beta3 + rho/looksam_sam/sg_rescale)
172	    st.lr = lr;
173	
174	    MambaTokenCtx tok;
175	    tok.tokens    = tokens;
176	    tok.targets   = targets;
177	    tok.B         = B;
178	    tok.workspace = sc.workspace;
179	    tok.loss_out  = loss_out;
180	
181	    // Dispatch to the matching kernel instantiation. The fwd+bwd is identical across
182	    // these OptIds; the template differs ONLY in the P3 apply_optimizer<Opt> tail.
183	    // Unsupported opt_ids return cudaErrorInvalidValue → dispatch.cpp throws LOUD.
184	    switch (static_cast<OptId>(opt_id)) {
185	        case OptId::AdamW:
186	            return launch_fused_mamba_megakernel_tc<OptId::AdamW>(
187	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
188	        case OptId::Lion:
189	            return launch_fused_mamba_megakernel_tc<OptId::Lion>(
190	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
191	        case OptId::Grokfast:
192	            return launch_fused_mamba_megakernel_tc<OptId::Grokfast>(
193	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
194	        case OptId::GrokAdamW:
195	            // 3-mechanism GrokAdamW (wave-2 mamba): the kernel's P2.5 global grad-norm
196	            // clip + P3 per-tensor layer-wise β1 land in fused_mamba_megakernel_tc<Opt>
197	            // (mirrors the decoder/vit TC kernels). γ/grad_clip thread through
198	            // FusedScalars (apply_scalars). ema = the `extra` slice (cold-start seed).
199	            return launch_fused_mamba_megakernel_tc<OptId::GrokAdamW>(
200	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
201	        case OptId::NeuralGrok:
202	            // psi-net MLP tail (wave-2 mamba): apply_optimizer<NeuralGrok> reads the
203	            // psi pack the host scattered into the `extra` slice (st.psi_W1/b1/W2 bound
204	            // above) + alpha/beta from FusedScalars. Pure elementwise — no precompute,
205	            // no cross-CTA reduction, so it inherits the deterministic grad reduce.
206	            return launch_fused_mamba_megakernel_tc<OptId::NeuralGrok>(
207	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
208	        case OptId::Prodigy:
209	            // STAGED global-d (wave-2 mamba): the SAME single persistent launch — the
210	            // cross-ALL-tensors d-estimate is an IN-KERNEL phase (P2.6, between the grad
211	            // reduce B2 and the apply P3), not a separate launch. st carries param_init/
212	            // prodigy_persist/d0/d_coef/beta3 (bound above); the mamba TC kernel decays+
213	            // accumulates the EMA, updates d, applies. The reduce slots are carved in
214	            // mb_tc_workspace_floats (mb_tc_opt_reduce_floats), so this scratch already fits.
215	            return launch_fused_mamba_megakernel_tc<OptId::Prodigy>(
216	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
217	        case OptId::LookSAM:
218	            // MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward (mamba SAM-tier lane): the SAME single
219	            // persistent launch — the perturb→2nd in-kernel fwd+bwd→sam_dir=g_sam−g is
220	            // an IN-KERNEL phase (P2.4, between B2 and P2.5/P3), gated to every-k SAM
221	            // steps by st.looksam_sam. The transient backup + g_sam buffers live in the
222	            // workspace (mb_tc_looksam_floats, carved after the Prodigy reduce slots);
223	            // sam_dir persists in the extra slice (st.sam_dir, bound above). The apply
224	            // tail (P3) blends g_adj=(1−α)g+α·sam_dir and runs AdamW. NOT a separate
225	            // launch. The decoder/vit twins proved this routing.
226	            return launch_fused_mamba_megakernel_tc<OptId::LookSAM>(
227	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
228	        case OptId::Muon:
229	            // STAGED grid-cooperative Newton-Schulz (mamba muon lane): the SAME single
230	            // persistent launch — the NS orthogonalization of the 13 2D weights (tok/pos/
231	            // A_log/in_proj/x_proj/dt_proj/out_proj × 2 layers + out.weight) is an IN-KERNEL
232	            // phase (P2.7, between B2/P2.6 and P3), grid-barrier-looped per matrix, NOT a
233	            // separate launch. The per-matrix NS scratch lives in the workspace
234	            // (mb_tc_muon_floats, carved after the LookSAM scratch). The persistent momentum
235	            // buffer is the m-slice (st.exp_avg, bound above); the 1D/non-2D weights take the
236	            // AdamW tail in P3 reading the INDEPENDENT aux_lr/aux_betas (eager Muon adamw_*
237	            // group, carried via apply_scalars). The decoder/vit twins proved this routing.
238	            // muon/mamba is a SINGLE forward + NS precompute (NOT a 2nd forward), so it does
239	            // NOT hit the shared mamba-forward A/A/A race that blocks the SAM-2nd-pass mamba
240	            // cells — VERIFIED A/A/A bit-exact by test_l3tc_tail_gate (muon/mamba).
241	            return launch_fused_mamba_megakernel_tc<OptId::Muon>(
242	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
243	        case OptId::SuperGrok11:
244	            // MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward + per-tensor meta-net mu/gate (mamba SAM-tier
245	            // lane): the SAME single persistent launch. The SAM 2nd backward (P2.4,
246	            // sharpness=(g_sam−g)²) + the per-tensor mu precompute (P3, mu=rescale·
247	            // phi(g,sharpness)) + the per-tensor cosine gate are ALL in-kernel phases; the
248	            // apply tail (sg11_sweep_b_step: smart_grad=g+(1−gate)·alpha·mu, AdamW) runs in
249	            // P3. The SAM scratch reuses the looksam buffers (mb_tc_looksam_floats);
250	            // sharpness + the phi pack ride the extended state buffer (bound above). The SAM
251	            // double-forward is now A/A/A bit-exact on mamba (the register-pressure wgmma-
252	            // accumulator-spill race is fixed; looksam/mamba proved it). NOT a separate launch.
253	            return launch_fused_mamba_megakernel_tc<OptId::SuperGrok11>(
254	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
255	        case OptId::SuperGrok15:
256	            // Same SAM 2nd backward + mu precompute as SG11, but SIMPLER tail: the gate is a
257	            // host scalar (st.gate = sigmoid(accuracy)), NO per-tensor cosine stage; the apply
258	            // tail (sg15_sweep_b_step) does the per-coord alpha clip + smart_grad = g +
259	            // gate·a·mu + AdamW. Single persistent launch.
260	            return launch_fused_mamba_megakernel_tc<OptId::SuperGrok15>(
261	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
262	        default:
263	            return cudaErrorInvalidValue;  // STAGED/coupled opt not single-launch TC
264	    }

272	// generic launcher + the byte-identical cells are UNTOUCHED). It binds the SG2 state
273	// slices, threads the weight bundle + scalar arrays through FusedOptState's sg2_* fields,
274	// and dispatches the OptId::SuperGrok2 kernel instantiation (its P3-SG2 phase runs
275	// sg2_meta_stages per tensor: STAGE -1 in-kernel segmented sort → CSA/HCA/GRU/PEER/apply,
276	// reading st.sharpness from the SAM 2nd backward (P2.4, shared with SG11/15)).
277	//
278	// STATE LAYOUT (host sizes it; this carves it):
279	//   [m(total) | v(total) | mu(total) | loss(1) | sharpness(total) | slow(total)
280	//    | gru_state(total*GH)]   ⇒ min_state = (4+1+GH)*total + 1   (GH=gru_hidden=4)
281	// perm/unsort are built IN-KERNEL into the per-CTA workspace (NOT state).
282	cudaError_t mega_mamba_sg2_tc(
283	        PersistentContext ctx, float* params,
284	        const int* tokens, const int* targets, int B,
285	        float* state, float* grad, float* loss_out,
286	        // SG2 meta-net weight bundle (HBM, fp32, model-independent), in SG2Weights order.
287	        const float* input_proj_W, const float* input_proj_b,
288	        const float* csa_q_W, const float* csa_k_W, const float* csa_v_W, const float* csa_out_W,
289	        const float* csa_compress_w, const float* csa_idx_DQ, const float* csa_idx_K,
290	        const float* hca_q_W, const float* hca_k_W, const float* hca_v_W, const float* hca_out_W,
291	        const float* gru_Wz, const float* gru_bz, const float* gru_Wr, const float* gru_br,
292	        const float* gru_Wh, const float* gru_bh,
293	        const float* peer_query_Ws, const float* prod_keys_A, const float* prod_keys_B,
294	        const float* expert_W1, const float* expert_b1, const float* expert_W2, const float* expert_b2,
295	        // per-tensor scalar arrays (device, length kMambaNumTensors).
296	        const float* sc_alpha, const float* sc_gru_decay, const float* sc_lamb_eff,
297	        const float* sc_beta1, const float* sc_bc1, const float* sc_bc2,
298	        // shared scalars + the SAM 2nd-backward gate (SG2 reuses the LookSAM P2.4 machinery).
299	        float rescale, float beta2, float lr, float wd, float eps,
300	        float rho, float sam_on,
301	        int step, cudaStream_t stream, int ncta_cap) {
302	    const int64_t total = kMambaTotalElems;
303	    const int T = B * mb::kSeq;
304	
305	    int dev = 0;
306	    cudaError_t err = cudaGetDevice(&dev);
307	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
308	    int n_sms = 1;
309	    err = cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&n_sms, cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount, dev);
310	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
311	    // Size the workspace for the EXACT count the kernel launcher runs (occ·n_sms with the
312	    // occupancy-fill default; reg-capped uniform across OptIds). Falls back to n_sms.
313	    int nCTA = mb_tc_launched_nctas<OptId::SuperGrok2>(dev, ncta_cap);
314	    if (nCTA <= 0) { nCTA = n_sms; if (ncta_cap > 0 && ncta_cap < nCTA) nCTA = ncta_cap; }
315	
316	    const int64_t need = mb_tc_workspace_floats(T, nCTA);
317	    MbTcLauncherScratch& sc = mb_tc_launcher_scratch(dev, need);
318	    ctx.g_next_task  = sc.g_next;
319	    ctx.g_arrived    = sc.g_arrived;
320	    ctx.g_generation = sc.g_generation;
321	    ctx.n_tasks      = kMambaNumTensors;
322	
323	    // Bind the SG2 state slices: [m | v | mu | loss | sharpness | slow | gru_state].
324	    FusedOptState st;
325	    st.exp_avg     = state;                       // m
326	    st.exp_avg_sq  = state + total;               // v
327	    st.mu          = state + 2 * total;           // expert-output EMA
328	    // loss_out points at state + 3*total (dispatch's loss slot).
329	    float* sharp_base = loss_out + 1;             // state + 3*total + 1
330	    st.sharpness   = sharp_base;                  // (g_sam − g)² (SAM 2nd backward, P2.4)
331	    st.sg2_slow    = sharp_base + total;          // grokfast slow-grad EMA
332	    st.sg2_gru_state = st.sg2_slow + total;       // [total*GH] per-element GRU state
333	    // meta-net weight bundle (HBM).
334	    st.sg2_input_proj_W = input_proj_W; st.sg2_input_proj_b = input_proj_b;
335	    st.sg2_csa_q_W = csa_q_W; st.sg2_csa_k_W = csa_k_W; st.sg2_csa_v_W = csa_v_W;
336	    st.sg2_csa_out_W = csa_out_W; st.sg2_csa_compress_w = csa_compress_w;
337	    st.sg2_csa_idx_DQ = csa_idx_DQ; st.sg2_csa_idx_K = csa_idx_K;
338	    st.sg2_hca_q_W = hca_q_W; st.sg2_hca_k_W = hca_k_W; st.sg2_hca_v_W = hca_v_W;
339	    st.sg2_hca_out_W = hca_out_W;
340	    st.sg2_gru_Wz = gru_Wz; st.sg2_gru_bz = gru_bz; st.sg2_gru_Wr = gru_Wr;
341	    st.sg2_gru_br = gru_br; st.sg2_gru_Wh = gru_Wh; st.sg2_gru_bh = gru_bh;
342	    st.sg2_peer_query_Ws = peer_query_Ws; st.sg2_prod_keys_A = prod_keys_A;
343	    st.sg2_prod_keys_B = prod_keys_B;
344	    st.sg2_expert_W1 = expert_W1; st.sg2_expert_b1 = expert_b1;
